A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DB-KSVD work. All 16 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison; retained experiments can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gemma-2-2B evaluations, runtime measurements, dictionary-coherence analyses and a synthetic experiment on initialization with partially known structure.

after.justification: v2 retains the Gemma experiments and reports additional Pythia-160M and DINOv2 evaluations, including quantitative comparisons and visual feature examples.

M1.justification: The dictionary-learning objective, accelerated matching pursuit, inner and outer batching, dictionary updates and Matryoshka procedure remain unchanged in Sections 2 and 4. Additional complexity analysis and applications do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet-1k vision coverage through DINOv2 embeddings, image-class probing and visual autointerpretability. It removes v1's noisy synthetic task with partially known coefficient structure. The Pile-based language task remains; adding Pythia within that task is principally a model-configuration expansion.

E2.justification: The SAEBench comparator set and original KSVD timing baseline remain. The new vision comparison evaluates a modified TopK-SAE comparator: Appendix B.2 uses matching pursuit with its learned dictionary instead of its encoder. TopK-SAE itself was already represented in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds Pythia-160M and DINOv2-S/B configurations. Its new vision protocol uses 4096 dictionary elements, sparsities 16/32/64, per-class logistic probes, and GPT-4o-mini explanations scored using CLIP and Spearman correlation. Matching pursuit controls encoding across vision dictionaries. The existing Gemma training protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's systematic study of known initialization fractions, including Figure 3 and Appendix A.2, is removed. v2 adds sensitivity to the number of probing features per class (Table 5) and image/feature interpretation case studies (Figures 3–4). The existing coherence and training-convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the fastest of five timing trials and state that trials fall within a 10% margin. Neither provides repeated-run uncertainty estimates for dictionary-quality comparisons; the added evaluation scores introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds five-metric Pythia results and DINOv2 results while removing the synthetic initialization findings. For DINOv2-B at k=32, Table 2 reports DB-KSVD versus SAE variance explained of 0.817 versus 0.794, probing accuracy of 0.893 versus 0.932, and autointerpretability of 0.802 versus 0.797. These are new comparisons; retained Gemma results and timing values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and new Appendix C extend v1's component-cost discussion into total computational and memory bounds, including Equation 8 and a cubic-scaling claim under stated parameter assumptions. This is an analytical extension; the optimization formulation, identifiability bounds and existing sample-complexity discussion remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion explicitly extend the empirical competitive-performance claim from Gemma to additional language and vision models. The central claims about scalable alternating optimization, Matryoshka structuring and SAE solution quality are retained.

C2.justification: v2 introduces interpretations concerning weaker SAE performance at lower embedding dimensions, saturation of visual explanations, and better isolation of individual concepts by SAE features. Appendix D.4 adds a qualified interpretation of existing curves as suggesting approximately 1.3 million samples for convergence. The discussion of benefits from partially known initialization disappears.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 documents CLS extraction, feature/image selection counts, the explanation prompt, scoring procedure and sign handling. Appendix C newly reports single-precision memory requirements, approximately 80 GB RAM and 16–32 GB GPU memory. Existing Gemma implementation details remain, while synthetic-data generation details are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Pythia, DINOv2, ImageNet, automated neuron explanations and Prisma. Citations to weakly supervised disentanglement, Barlow Twins and VICReg disappear with the initialization study. The main related-work narrative and positioning relative to KSVD and SAEs remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 refines introductory and theoretical explanations, converts contribution bullets to an inline enumeration, and places benchmark and coherence results before timing results. Appendices are reorganized around visualization, experimental details, complexity and additional results. Most existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with extensive resizing and relocation of retained displays. v2 adds visual feature panels, a Pythia results figure and three vision-result tables, while removing the synthetic convergence figure. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens applicability evidence beyond v1's single real-world embedding source by testing another language model and two vision models, revealing reconstruction–probing tradeoffs and providing inspectable feature examples. The shared matching-pursuit control and added resource documentation improve assessment of dictionary quality and feasibility. Removing the initialization study loses useful evidence, and quality-score uncertainty remains unreported, but the broader validation provides a substantial net gain.
